findings.issue: The B6 selector's `:not(TSModuleDeclaration > .id)` exclusion (spec 5 and 7 say `declare global { … }` must stay allowed) is not exercised by any probe. Deleting it from the selector would not fail this test, and no real file under src/bots or src/advice uses `declare global`, so the lintFiles check would not catch it either.
findings.evidence: CLEAN_PROBE contains class constructor, object keys, o.global and interface members, but no `declare global`. An in-memory run confirmed `declare global { interface Window { x: number } }` lints clean today. SPEC-04's literal probe text also leaves it out, so this is a test gap, not a spec violation.

findings.issue: `:not(TSModuleDeclaration > .id)` is appended to the `Function` selector too, where it only matters for an unrealistic `declare module Function`/`namespace Function`. Spec 5 lists it in the shared exclusions, so this matches the spec.
findings.fix: Optional: keep it as is for symmetry with the global selector.

summary: The implementation matches spec 5 exactly: B1-B6 are separate no-restricted-syntax entries in BOT_DETERMINISM_RESTRICTED_SYNTAX, B7/B8 are globalThis.Function/global property bans, the messages match A-4 word for word, and the NAME_ONLY_POSITIONS refactor keeps BARE_GLOBAL_REFERENCE's selector identical (same :not set, order only). The acceptance test passes (4/4). I ran an in-memory mutation check on the probe sets by removing each of B1..B8 in turn from the loaded config: every removal makes at least 2 probe assertions fail, so SPEC-05 holds. Edge cases also checked: fn?.constructor is flagged, `declare global` passes, and new Function is reported by both no-new-func and B5 as the spec expects. Gates pass (lint, typecheck, tests, scope 176/190 lines, 2/2 files). No BLOCKER or MAJOR. One MINOR: the `declare global` exclusion has no probe.
